title: I Posted the Neighborhood Tool-Share Photo the Thief Already Liked

parts.text: I lent a cordless drill to the tool-share thread on Tuesday. Thursday it was on Nextdoor Marketplace with my scratch on the battery, liked by the borrower, Chris. I was forty, standing in my garage that smelled like sawdust and rain. I screenshotted the listing, the like, and the original thread where Chris wrote I'll bring it back Friday. Friday he said he got robbed. The listing was still up at 4 p.m. I commented on the Marketplace post with the scratch photo. Then Chris messaged: take it down, my cousin listed it by mistake.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The cousin excuse arrived while his like was still on my drill.

social.video_title: He liked the listing of the drill he borrowed — Part 1/2
social.description: Tool-share, a scratch on the battery, and a Friday robbery that could still add to cart. Would you have commented in public?

parts.text: I did not take it down. I asked him to bring the drill or the cousin to my garage. Chris arrived at 6 with the drill and a story that changed twice. I took the drill, posted RETURNED in the thread, and left the Marketplace screenshot up for twenty-four hours because that is how long his like existed. The tool-share added a photo log. Chris does not borrow. My battery still has the scratch. I know it on sight. Sawdust is honest. Likes are evidence.

social.video_title: He returned it with a story that could not sit still — Part 2/2
social.description: Garage handoff, photo log, like as a receipt. Was a cousin a listing agent?
